title: How many stories does a typical student read?
description: Fifteen students' story counts include one very large value, and the board finds the mean and the median with and without it. Keeko doubts that the middle of the list as written is the median.
teaching_notes: One idea: the median needs sorting first, and a high outlier lifts the mean above it. Watch for children who take the middle of the list as written.

video_script.why: The child has met outliers and the median and now handles fifteen unsorted values.
video_script.substitution: Sort first, then count to the middle; the outlier sits at the very end.
video_script.wrong_move: takes the eighth value of the list as written, which is seven, instead of sorting first
video_script.payoff_line: The mean falls by much more than the median

final_answer.value: mean 8.13 and median 6; without 40, mean 5.86 and median 5.5
final_answer.spoken: the mean is about eight point one three and the median is six; without the outlier, the mean is about five point eight six and the median is five point five

hold_back: The mean falls by much more than the median
maths_rules: without 40: total 82, 14 values, mean 5.86 (to two places), median (5 + 6) / 2 = 5.5
the mean fell by about 2.27; the median fell by 0.5
video_script.design: One idea: sort before the middle. Fifteen story cards stay in the anchor; they sort into a row on the stage; an outlier card flies off at the end.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; fifteen slips of paper in a row, each with the number of short stories read by one student

marks.m1: the title card From your book appears
marks.m2: a teacher stands beside a classroom of fifteen students
marks.m3: fifteen slips of paper with numbers slide in
marks.m4: a question mark rises over the slips

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is an example from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>After the summer holidays, a teacher asks fifteen students how many short stories they read.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Their answers are on fifteen slips of paper.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>How many stories does a typical student read?

beats.on_screen: the fifteen slips stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child who is thinking

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two labels appear under the slips: mean and median; a question asks what one far value will do to them

marks.g1: the labels mean and median appear under the slips
marks.g2: the slip with 40 is circled and a small question mark appears beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Two numbers can stand for the group, the mean and the median.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>We will find both, and then see what one far value does to them.

marks.given: the heading stories read by fifteen students is written
marks.g2: the first eight counts are written in a row
marks.g3: the last seven counts are written after them

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the stories read by fifteen students were as follows.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Six, eight, five, fifteen, three, zero, two and seven.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>Then twelve, forty, ten, five, zero, eight and one.

beats.on_screen: To find: the mean and the median, then again without the outlier

marks.find: the words without the outlier are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the mean and the median, and then find them again without the outlier.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, mean = total ÷ number of students: total 122; 122 ÷ 15 ≈ 8.13 stories

marks.s1: the rule mean = total ÷ number of students is written
marks.s2: the fifteen counts add up to 122

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, add all the counts and share the total over fifteen students.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>The total is one hundred and twenty two stories.
<bookmark mark='s3'/>One hundred and twenty two divided by fifteen is about eight point one three.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, median: sorted 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8, 10, 12, 15, 40; the 8th value is 6

marks.d1: the fifteen slips sort from smallest to largest
marks.d2: the first eight sorted counts are shown in a row
marks.d3: the last seven sorted counts are shown after them
marks.d4: the 8th count, 6, is circled with seven on each side

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step two, sort the counts from smallest to largest.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Zero, zero, one, two, three, five, five and six.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>Then seven, eight, eight, ten, twelve, fifteen and forty.
<bookmark mark='d4'/>There are fifteen values, so the eighth one has seven on each side.
The median is six stories.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, leave out the outlier 40: total 82 in 14 values, mean 82 ÷ 14 ≈ 5.86; median (5 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5.5

marks.e1: the 40 slip flies off the row
marks.e2: the fourteen counts left add up to 82
marks.e4: the 7th and 8th counts, 5 and 6, are circled and the mark halfway reads 5.5

narration: <bookmark mark='e1'/>Step three, forty is far above the rest, so it is the outlier.
<bookmark mark='e2'/>Leave it out, and fourteen values remain, adding up to eighty two.
<bookmark mark='e3'/>Eighty two divided by fourteen gives a new mean of about five point eight six.
<bookmark mark='e4'/>Fourteen values have two in the middle, five and six.
The new median is five point five.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, compare the changes: mean 8.13 to 5.86, a fall of about 2.27; median 6 to 5.5, a fall of 0.5

marks.f1: the old and the new numbers are placed side by side
marks.f2: the mean gauge falls by about 2.27

narration: <bookmark mark='f1'/>Step four, compare the changes.
<bookmark mark='f2'/>The mean fell by about two point two seven stories.
<bookmark mark='f3'/>The median fell by only half a story.

beats.on_screen: Answer: mean ≈ 8.13 and median 6; without 40, mean ≈ 5.86 and median 5.5; the mean falls by much more than the median

marks.ans2: the two new numbers 5.86 and 5.5 are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The mean falls by much more than the median.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>Without the outlier, the mean is about five point eight six.
The median is five point five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's thought bubble shows the fifteen slips as written with the eighth slip, 7, lit up; then the slips sort and the middle slip changes to 6

marks.doubt: the bubble with the unsorted slips and the lit eighth slip, 7, appears
marks.fix: the slips are shown in the order the students answered, with the 40 and the 0s scattered
marks.idea: the slips sort and the middle slip becomes 6

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the median is seven, because seven is the eighth number in the list.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The list is in the order the students answered, not in order of size.
<bookmark mark='idea'/>Sort first, then count to the middle.
